text: The authors state Theorem 5.1 informally: for arbitrary U in M, they define the population expansion c(U) = P(n(x) in U | x in A)/P(x in U | x in B) and its empirical estimate c-hat(U), the fraction of the n_A samples from A with n(x_i) in U divided by the fraction of the n_B samples from B that lie in U. The quoted lines then break off at the start of the theorem's guarantee, which holds for any delta in (0, 1] with a probability that is cut off.
title: Theorem 5.1: empirical vs population expansion estimates (expansion generalization)
